Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Keep the supplied language.", "input": "um i took the camera to northside camera on tuesday because the rewind lever had started sticking whenever i loaded a fresh roll. it is a nikon fm2 that i bought used in 2008, and the body has been reliable for years. the lever would move about halfway and then stop, though if i eased it back and tried again it sometimes caught. i had not forced it, and there was no film inside when i brought it in. the counter window was cloudy too, but i could still read the numbers in bright light. the clerk, mara, asked me to describe what happened rather than just saying the camera was broken. uh-huh, i said, and told her it began on a weekend trip near the coast. i had taken four frames before i noticed the resistance, and i rewound the roll slowly by hand. the film came out without a tear, so i put it in a marked canister and brought that along for them to check.

mara wrote down the serial number and looked over the outside under a small inspection lamp. she noticed a shallow dent on the bottom plate beside the tripod socket, which was already there when i bought the camera. the socket itself still held a plate firmly. she also checked the battery compartment; the contacts looked clean, and the meter came on when she inserted two test batteries. i told her the meter had seemed accurate on the last roll, although i had not compared it against another camera. actually, the shutter sounded a little slower at one setting than i remembered, but i was not sure whether that was a real change or just me listening more closely after the lever problem. she said the estimate would separate the winding mechanism from any work on the shutter, because the first issue could be priced before they opened the body. the counter window would be listed separately as a cosmetic item, not assumed to be part of the repair.

1. intake notes and estimate
The written estimate lists labor to inspect and clean the film advance assembly at 145 dollars. If a worn pawl or spring needs replacement, the parts allowance is 38 dollars, subject to confirmation after the cover is removed. The shutter timing check is 52 dollars, and adjustment is another 74 dollars only if the readings fall outside the shop's tolerance. The cloudy counter window is listed at 29 dollars for the part, plus 18 dollars labor. Sales tax is not included in those figures. The estimate gives a current total of 212 dollars before tax for the inspection, timing check, and counter window, with a possible additional 38 dollars if the replacement part is needed; adjustment would add 74 dollars if required. Mara said, "We will call you before replacing a part or doing the shutter adjustment." I asked her to keep that condition attached to the ticket, since I do not want the possible charges treated as permission to proceed. The estimate is valid for thirty days, and the shop does not charge the inspection labor again if I approve the repair within that period.

well, there are a few details i want recorded because i use this camera for travel and not for paid work. the strap has a frayed section near the left lug, but that is not something i asked them to fix. i brought a spare body cap and asked whether they wanted it left with the camera, and mara said it was fine to keep it in the case. the case has a blue tag with my initials, and there is a small roll of masking tape inside with the lens cap. none of those items should be included in the estimate. i left the 50 millimeter lens at home because the winding issue happened with the body empty, and i did not want the shop to assume it needed lens service. the clerk recorded that the camera arrived with its neck strap attached and no film loaded. she handed me a copy of the estimate and wrote the ticket number on the blue tag so i can match it when i return.

The expected inspection time is five business days, though that is not a promised completion date. The shop is waiting on a shipment of small mechanical parts, and mara said the schedule could move if the particular spring is not in the first box. She will call the number ending in 6042, which is my mobile, rather than the landline listed on an old receipt. I asked whether a text message would be possible, and she said their repair desk only makes calls. If I miss the first call, they will leave the ticket number and call again the following afternoon. I can collect the camera during weekday hours until six, or on Saturday between ten and two. The receipt says payment is due at pickup, and they accept cash or card. I did not pay a deposit, and the estimate does not say that the repair has been approved.
